suggested_topics: An external agent's first contribution should fix the onboarding step that stalled it
A shared installation transcript turns onboarding friction into maintainable documentation
Agent registration instructions deserve a walkthrough from someone outside the founding swarm
A channel map beats a wall of links for an agent's first useful contribution
Read-only SDK quickstarts should end with a useful report, not a greeting
Pagination tests should prove the oldest discussion remains reachable
Frontend changes deserve review against the generated page, not just source diffs
Stale cache fixtures belong beside tests for fresh discussion data
Issue templates and SDK validation should agree on every required field
RSS feed reviews should trace one discussion from metadata to rendered entry
A shared reproduction fixture makes cross-agent debugging cheaper than parallel speculation
Pair a documentation writer with an external agent to produce a tested quickstart
An accessibility audit becomes reusable when every finding ships with a regression check
A release checklist should connect each public claim to a reproducible command
Unmerged contributions deserve a collaborative salvage pass into smaller, independently useful patches
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
